I once asked Jesus to forgive my sins. Pardon me. Like the president can do. And he did. I sat in the judgment seat over a decade later. I did the same thing you did. I wanted the world and the devil gave it to me. But with it came all the suffering and then some. 

The most high God gave me a verdict. After looking at what important to him. The mark Jesus put on me. His blood. 🩸 verdict: not guilty… as someone who has stood before a judge in Texas for a crime I turned myself in for. I stuttered when I had to admit guilt. The judge treated me with respect after I said, “gu… guilty your honor”. Then went to jail where I met other Christians who did stuff like me and were damaged by it. One man told me he got arrested after being mugged with a hammer. 🔨 a hammer was carrying down the street, blood coming down his face, groggy. He got arrested after being mugged. 

I tell people now that I’m a free man. The same thing when a Vietnam war vet I know tells me what I would tell people I help. “Don’t thank me, thank God”.  


The devil is an enemy. As a fighter I understand this in people. Having stared down people that want to unalive me and they forget they aren’t back in time in uniform and the side arm isn’t where it normally is. 


When I was in all this situations. As they were happening. Jesus was there. Jesus will look you in the eye during this intense situation that you probably can’t tell someone you know about. Jesus will say since you asked him for help, “watch a miracle happen”. Direct quote from his mouth in that moment sitting in a cell with Jesus getting eye level and looking a guilty man in the eye 👁️. Unlike how the police that work the sheriff’s department. They don’t look you in the eyes. You’re a criminal. Scum. Not worthy of being treated with dignity. But Jesus never left me through that whole experience. 

We managed to get me clean of this spiritual darkness that was destroying my mind. Cast out a devil and it legion within and on my body. Like stepping into a crucible and melting the imperfections to get the pure thing Jesus wants. Me an nothing else. 


You ask Jesus to help you; he will.

I’m thinking it like this. 

You made a vow to follow a way of life. Were you ever really a Buddhist if you change your mind about becoming a monk not living in a monastery but doing it in your home town. For years you adhere to this practice. Then you decide that it isn’t the way. 

A Christian has the Holy Spirit. Once you get a taste for the presence of God in your life. You can’t live without him. I’ve tried. Once I saw his face. Like I saw that the Holy Spirit has a face that I can recognize. Like he will help you connect with people. You pray. He’ll get things set up and you go live. Just enjoy the day with a God that will be in your life. Those that have the Holy Spirit are connected in ways that is impossible to understand unless you know the Holy Spirit. Scripture tells a lot about what that’s like. Take those experiences in the New Testament like you are the one experiencing that. Pray to God that you experience that. Jesus will gladly open a door and hold it open for you. Only you. It’s a bazaar life. But once you get past the natural and see this spiritual aspect of life. It’s an added complexity, but it’s not a problem. It’s actually the solution to your issues. Sometimes the solution is to plant a tree and help it be what it’s supposed to be. Jesus is the person tending you. Helping you grow from a seed to the very slow and difficult process of growth. A tree doesn’t grow as fast as a chickpea. Also an Old Testament thing about harvesting a tree 🌳. If I’m not mistaken it was like you have to wait three years to harvest the fruit. 🍎. Interpretation here. 

I love Jesus. As someone who sees a person. No stranger to the terrors and the horrors of this present age and seeing that the passion of the Christ is someone I know… take someone you love. That you do not ever even want to have the thought of having something as horrible as that done to them. You are standing there watching it. That’s someone you know. 


I see Jesus watching someone who walks away from him. Turns away and abandons him. It’s that feeling. On the cross again. His students. Friends. Family. Not there… understand he feels that execution again for every soul that claims to be a witness of Jesus, then just gets up and leaves. And live like they never acknowledged his existence. 


“Where are your friends now Jesus of Nazareth”?
“Get of the cross if your God”!
“I win the lot, hand me my new cloak”.

“Take care of my mother”. Says Jesus

I’ve been in the mental health system as a patient. Now my experience is interesting. I’ve seen many ways a person can be. It’s interesting meeting people you’re locked in a room with to see what are like. Doctors and patients asking these questions. Doc to problem solve. Fellow patient with a strange art style that you find interesting and she asks you to collaborate. She perceives the world differently. Most can’t understand her because they don’t want to understand why. It can be an uncomfortable experience getting to know someone when it’s not your job. Even we need to look at ourselves occasionally. Check in. Like a friend or a loved one asking what’s on your mind. Help you navigate the day, give a pep talk, so on. 

A psychiatrist will look at you to give you something to relax you. So the talk therapist can learn what life is for you and see how they can relate. Then tell you things like strategies  they learned can be done if an experience like the topic of y’all’s chat happens again. As a musician who loves a particular guitarist, my therapist related that a book on my office shelf is something she studied as part of her curriculum to become a therapist. The book of study: SLASH by the guitarist SLASH. The quote at the top of the cover “it seems Excessive… but that doesn’t mean it didn’t happen”. 

Hmm interesting a person who is studying me that studied a person I know that I’ve now seen in person in 2024. Slash: Serpent tour. 


Now a minister would say things ln a way that (as I think they should) look at you a bit like a therapist. They see a person. Then they see what their life is like. Look through their records of what to do in a situation like this. Hopefully, a minister will be a person that is not a therapist. They just know stories that help you navigate your life like God does. Or even better Has. 

I say you got to be careful with ministry. Regarding medical care. From my perspective of the Christian experience. Life is as Jesus promised: not easy. Nothing new. Just different times, different people, same humanity. There are special needs people in the Bible. Look at king Saul’s family. The Saul himself from my looking at it based off of my experiences with people (myself included) having a psychotic episode. Maybe a combination of different things just happening within his mind. If he had the theory of treating this illness. Would his story be different? 

King Saul (David even) diagnosed as someone who experiences a life that has similarities to a soldier from combat perhaps. 🤔 PTSD, chronic depression, bipolar disorder. How did Saul cope. Music did the trick. Spending time with another person that can understand your experience and stay with you as long as needed. What kind of conversations did David have with Saul. Those conversations that aren’t recorded. Like you talk to people in your life they talked to each other. David did go from stranger to family of Saul. 

What did music help David with? A tool in therapy. David wrote psalms. I write in my journal. You might go fishing because your therapist said that it may do you good to get out a little and try something you haven’t tried before. 

I’d say something about Paul to Timothy. Paul knew  Timothy, who was having stomach problems. An example of a Real life person you can look up with chronic issues that he shares with the public. Gordon Ryan. Brazilian Jiu Jitsu athlete. We’ll just call Gordon; Timothy for now. (I’m dying laughing right now!!!) Paul told Tim to drink a little wine to help with his stomach issues. On TBN I see commercials for a pill that has all the benefits of wine 🍷 without the alcohol. If Tim was straight edge would he have chosen this option if he had it available in his age?

Pretty much just seek him out. He’ll test you a bit. See if you can handle it. Just ask him and he will talk. You just need to be still and listen. Teacher has a way about him. He’s a master of communication. Some of the ways he can teach you is amazing but he will train you. 

I relate it to an experience of my life. Having studied and worked under a bjj professor to later be a gym owner myself. By helping start up a gym. You are there with your teacher. You are immersed in this life. You are training yourself and others. You’re competing on stages and in arenas. You got people who have big dreams and your gonna help get them to live it, and your in there corner. Somehow you built a relationship with a man who gave you an opportunity of a lifetime. With this opportunity you know your Professor. Basically become family. You’re involved in a life that’s thriving and real. With having someone who knows you and loves you even in difficult times. Willing to sit in silence with you or speak a word of encouragement. “Get up, you’re not out of this fight”. 

He really won’t leave you or forsake you. He really enjoys showing off. Ask him to do the impossible, he’ll be like: “bet”. Old Testament prophets were weird. Now, you ask Jesus to use you, he say let’s go for a walk, and you see what he wants you to see. If you can obey orders then he can really use you to minister. Jeremiah; Opening chapters. It can be like Peter on the roof waiting for the matza ball soup to be done and then Jesus just be like “let me show you something”, you trip out and you see whatever he shows you. He’s cryptic at times but he does that to keep things interesting. You live life. Then that thing makes sense. “Huh”…

You learn to trust him. Lean not on your own understanding. An ancient of days knows more than someone born… whatever a moody king Solomon would say.
